sourceEvidence.text: Banana was used in English for the fruit in the late sixteenth century and later for its plant. Etymonline connects Spanish or Portuguese borrowing with a West African fruit-name and treats Wolof as a possibility. This supports a fruit-name borrowing, not an English root split. It does not settle the exact African donor language.

sourceEvidence.text: Oxford places the borrowing through Portuguese or Spanish and identifies a Mande source in West Africa. Etymonline instead proposes a possible Wolof connection. The shared, bounded account is a fruit-name transmitted through Iberian languages from West Africa; these sources do not justify selecting one African language as undisputed.
